verdict.text: The change does what the plan says.
Hermes selects an `openviking_tools` provider that subclasses the upstream plugin with writes forced off, startup session recovery skipped, empty `prefetch` and a static prompt block.
SOUL.md loses its Session Bootstrap and Auto-Capture sections.
The Claude Code how-to now removes the memory plugin.
The tag moves to 0.22.2-2.
The gates are green and the tests fail when the behavior breaks.
Row r7 can't run yet: it is a post-deploy check.
Gates rerun from the worktree: `just pre_commit` passed every hook, and `uv run --directory cli pytest` passed (666 passed, 21 deselected).
`loopctl gate stamp` result: pass on gates pre_commit and cli_tests and on rows r1 to r6, "stamp green: 1d1a3253c8f4df3369d95201d0359b6f7a82251ab7d927bed63e6d1086a44126".
The gates left no unstaged changes in the tree.
Upstream source: I pulled plugin 2.1.1 and `agent/memory_manager.py` from the local `ghcr.io/jasperhg90/hermes:0.22.2-1` image and checked the wrapper against them.
`_NON_PRIMARY_AGENT_CONTEXTS` includes `flush`, and `_agent_context` affects only `_writes_enabled`.
That flag gates `sync_turn`, `on_session_end`, every commit path in `on_session_switch`, `on_memory_write`, and the atexit safety net (which calls `on_session_end`).
`queue_prefetch` is already a no-op upstream.
Both calls to `_recover_pending_sessions` (in `initialize` and in the runtime re-attach path) hit the no-op override.
Upstream defines no `on_pre_compress`.
The tool handlers ignore the flag, so the `daily-blog-scrape` cron still reaches `viking_add_resource`.
The `name` override was added after spike 2, which showed name='openviking'.
In Hermes 0.22.2, a memory provider's `name` is used only for logs, the one-external-provider collision check, the unused `get_provider`, and telemetry.
Upstream never reads `self.name`.
Overriding it is safe.
Rows r1 to r6: I read each test against its `fails_when`.

To check that the tests can fail, I copied the wrapper into the scratchpad and broke it four ways, then ran the test file against each copy: without the `initialize` override, r1 fails ([primary]); without the `_recover_pending_sessions` override, r2 fails; without the `prefetch` override, r1 fails; without the `system_prompt_block` override, r1 and the prompt test fail.
r3 compares schemas to the stand-in's upstream list and checks that a `viking_search` request reaches the client.
r4 pins the provider line, checks that no `openviking:` or `recall_` keys remain, that the one COPY line is right and that the tag is 0.22.2-2.
r5 checks the SOUL.md headings.
r6 runs the skeleton check over every how-to plus a new test for the page: no install.sh, the uninstall commands present, a Check step, and a link to the CLI page.
r7 (judgment, not yet runnable, post-deploy): the plan can produce the evidence.

`ov_auth_proxy.py` logs each request line to stderr (`log_message`), so after the deploy `nomad alloc logs -stderr -task ov-auth-proxy` over a plain Telegram turn followed by `/new` should show only the `GET /health` from startup.
Then an explicit "search OpenViking for X" should show one `POST /api/v1/search/find`.
`hermes memory status` should name `openviking_tools`.
Spike 2 already showed this in the real 0.22.2-1 image with a stub upstream.
Consistency: hermes.md, ADR 0020, log.md, the summary ack, the docs indexes and the CLI how-to back-link all agree with the code.
No doc page, okf concept or summary still describes recall budgets, the memory plugin install, or the SOUL bootstrap and capture habits.
The how-to passes the skeleton test.
None.
r7 needs the operator.
The plan says the agent's Nomad token gets 403 on `nomad alloc logs` for `ov-auth-proxy`, and I see no recorded pre-deploy baseline.
Neither stops the judgment: r7's fails_when is about requests seen after the deploy, so no baseline is needed.
But someone with log access has to read the proxy stderr in a quiet window.
A cron run (`daily-blog-scrape` at 08:00) or the dashboard could add request lines that are not from the chat turn under test.
I could not run `kmctl check`: no `kmctl` binary in this environment.
The new test pins exactly one `COPY` line in the Dockerfile.
A future COPY will need that test updated.
That is a deliberate tight pin, not a defect.
